worked_solution:
For an initial value problem

$$
{y}^{′}=f(x,y),\,y(a)=c,
$$

the $2$-Step Adams-Bashforth-Moulton (ABM $2$-step) Method with step size $Δx$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Predictor} & : & Δ{y}_{p} & =\frac{1}{2}(3{y}^{′}-{y}_{-1}^{′})\cdot Δx, \\ \text{Corrector} & : & Δy & =\frac{1}{12}(5{y}_{p}^{′}+8{y}^{′}-{y}_{-1}^{′})\cdot Δx,\end{aligned}
$$

where

- ${y}^{′}=f(x,y)$ is the estimated slope at the current point $(x,y),$

- ${y}_{-1}^{′}=f({x}_{-1},{y}_{-1})$ is the estimated slope at the previous point (${x}_{-1},{y}_{-1}),$ and

- ${y}_{p}^{′}=f({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{p})$ is the estimated slope at the predicted new point $({x}_{\text{new}},{y}_{p})=(x+Δx,y+Δ{y}_{p}).$

Before we start, let's add the initial condition data and Runge-Kutta step data to a table.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}^{′}$ | $Δy$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $2$ |  | $-$ | $-$ | $-$ | $-$ |
| $2$ | $-\frac{9}{2}$ |  |  |  |  |  |

Now, since we want to find the value of $y$ at $x=3,$ we will use a step size of

$$
Δx=3-2=1.
$$

First, we compute the values of ${y}^{′}$ at each point according to the given rule:

- The slope at the previous point $({x}_{-1},{y}_{-1})=(1,2)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{-1}^{′} & ={x}_{-1}-{y}_{-1}-10 \\  & =1-2-10 \\  & =-11.\end{aligned}
$$

- The slope at the current point $(x,y)=(2,-\frac{9}{2})$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =x-y-10 \\  & =2-(-\frac{9}{2})-10 \\  & =-\frac{7}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We add these values to our table.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}^{′}$ | $Δy$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $2$ | $-11$ | $-$ | $-$ | $-$ | $-$ |
| $2$ | $-\frac{9}{2}$ | $-\frac{7}{2}$ |  |  |  |  |

Next, we compute $Δ{y}_{p}$ using the predictor equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}Δ{y}_{p} & =\frac{1}{2}(3{y}^{′}-{y}_{-1}^{′})\cdot Δx \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(3\cdot (-\frac{7}{2})-(-11))\cdot 1 \\  & =\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

We add this to our table.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}^{′}$ | $Δy$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $2$ | $-11$ | $-$ | $-$ | $-$ | $-$ |
| $2$ | $-\frac{9}{2}$ | $-\frac{7}{2}$ | $\frac{1}{4}$ |  |  |  |

So, the coordinates of the predicted new point are

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{\text{new}} & =x+Δx=2+1=3, \\ {y}_{p} & =y+Δ{y}_{p}=-\frac{9}{2}+\frac{1}{4}=-\frac{17}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Let's add the second value to the table.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}^{′}$ | $Δy$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $2$ | $-11$ | $-$ | $-$ | $-$ | $-$ |
| $2$ | $-\frac{9}{2}$ | $-\frac{7}{2}$ | $\frac{1}{4}$ | $-\frac{17}{4}$ |  |  |

Hence, the slope at this predicted point is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{p}^{′} & ={x}_{\text{new}}-{y}_{p}-10 \\  & =3-(-\frac{17}{4})-10 \\  & =-\frac{11}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can add this to our table.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}^{′}$ | $Δy$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $2$ | $-11$ | $-$ | $-$ | $-$ | $-$ |
| $2$ | $-\frac{9}{2}$ | $-\frac{7}{2}$ | $\frac{1}{4}$ | $-\frac{17}{4}$ | $-\frac{11}{4}$ |  |

Finally, we compute $Δy$ using the corrector equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}Δy & =\frac{1}{12}(5{y}_{p}^{′}+8{y}^{′}-{y}_{-1}^{′})\cdot Δx \\  & =\frac{1}{12}(5\cdot (-\frac{11}{4})+8\cdot (-\frac{7}{2})-(-11))\cdot 1 \\  & =\frac{1}{12}\cdot (-\frac{123}{4}) \\  & =-\frac{41}{16}.\end{aligned}
$$

We add this to our table.

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}^{′}$ | $Δy$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $2$ | $-11$ | $-$ | $-$ | $-$ | $-$ |
| $2$ | $-\frac{9}{2}$ | $-\frac{7}{2}$ | $\frac{1}{4}$ | $-\frac{17}{4}$ | $-\frac{11}{4}$ | $-\frac{41}{16}$ |

The value of $x$ in the next row is ${x}_{\text{new}}=3.$ To get the value of $y$ in the next row, we add $Δy$ to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{\text{new}} & =y+Δy \\  & =-\frac{9}{2}+(-\frac{41}{16}) \\  & =-\frac{113}{16}.\end{aligned}
$$

Adding these results to our table gives the following:

| $\,x\,$ | $\,y\,$ | $\,{y}^{′}\,$ | $Δ{y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}$ | ${y}_{p}^{′}$ | $Δy$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $1$ | $2$ | $-11$ | $-$ | $-$ | $-$ | $-$ |
| $2$ | $-\frac{9}{2}$ | $-\frac{7}{2}$ | $\frac{1}{4}$ | $-\frac{17}{4}$ | $-\frac{11}{4}$ | $-\frac{41}{16}$ |
| $3$ | $-\frac{113}{16}$ |  |  |  |  |  |

Therefore, we conclude that $y(3)≈-\frac{113}{16}.$
html:
For an initial value problem y′=f(x,y),y(a)=c, the 2-Step Adams-Bashforth-Moulton (ABM 2-step) Method with step size Δx is given by Predictor:Δyp=12(3y′−y−1′)⋅Δx,Corrector:Δy=112(5yp′+8y′−y−1′)⋅Δx, where

  • y′=f(x,y) is the estimated slope at the current point (x,y),

  • y−1′=f(x−1,y−1) is the estimated slope at the previous point (x−1,y−1), and

  • yp′=f(xnew,yp) is the estimated slope at the predicted new point (xnew,yp)=(x+Δx,y+Δyp).

Before we start, let's add the initial condition data and Runge-Kutta step data to a table.

x y y′ Δyp yp yp′ Δy
1 2 − − − −
2 −92

Now, since we want to find the value of y at x=3, we will use a step size of Δx=3−2=1.

First, we compute the values of y′ at each point according to the given rule:

  • The slope at the previous point (x−1,y−1)=(1,2) is y−1′=x−1−y−1−10=1−2−10=−11.

  • The slope at the current point (x,y)=(2,−92) is y′=x−y−10=2−(−92)−10=−72.

We add these values to our table.

x y y′ Δyp yp yp′ Δy
1 2 −11 − − − −
2 −92 −72

Next, we compute Δyp using the predictor equation:

Δyp=12(3y′−y−1′)⋅Δx=12(3⋅(−72)−(−11))⋅1=14.

We add this to our table.

x y y′ Δyp yp yp′ Δy
1 2 −11 − − − −
2 −92 −72 14

So, the coordinates of the predicted new point are xnew=x+Δx=2+1=3,yp=y+Δyp=−92+14=−174.

Let's add the second value to the table.

x y y′ Δyp yp yp′ Δy
1 2 −11 − − − −
2 −92 −72 14 −174

Hence, the slope at this predicted point is yp′=xnew−yp−10=3−(−174)−10=−114.

We can add this to our table.

x y y′ Δyp yp yp′ Δy
1 2 −11 − − − −
2 −92 −72 14 −174 −114

Finally, we compute Δy using the corrector equation:

Δy=112(5yp′+8y′−y−1′)⋅Δx=112(5⋅(−114)+8⋅(−72)−(−11))⋅1=112⋅(−1234)=−4116.

We add this to our table.

x y y′ Δyp yp yp′ Δy
1 2 −11 − − − −
2 −92 −72 14 −174 −114 −4116

The value of x in the next row is xnew=3. To get the value of y in the next row, we add Δy to y: ynew=y+Δy=−92+(−4116)=−11316.

Adding these results to our table gives the following:

x y y′ Δyp yp yp′ Δy
1 2 −11 − − − −
2 −92 −72 14 −174 −114 −4116
3 −11316

Therefore, we conclude that y(3)≈−11316.
